license: MIT (LICENSE, Copyright (c) 2026 Daniil Ostashev, added in c6893aa24ec2b2822ef42ab695c828de1ccb9015); the README says it covers the verification code and the record packings and certificates. The retained files are byte-identical with the licence beside them. Issue #575 credits Daniil Ostashev with the four packings, asks that the seeds' authors (Francisco Couzo, Evan Daniel, Joost de Winter) and the composition pieces' sources be acknowledged, and states AI assistance: an AI-assisted research loop the author drives with his own ideas, in which AI agents wrote and ran the search and verification code and an agent extended the band-merging move from the author's compositions to published two-band packings.
claims: Issue #575 reports s(176) <= 13.79587231843640726331185405391207744387, s(211) <= 14.99369418658324657063591818176125142354, s(241) <= 15.98713424905084041461665739745571396866 and, added on 2026-10-13, s(304) <= 17.92942775807517496566632613898911486244, certified and rounded up; each records/n0NNN.sqcert gives the exact side, dilated by 1 + 1e-60 from the 60-digit optimum of its contact topology, and the README at the pin prints the same sides rounded up to 15 places.

The issue says all four are new arrangements: at 176, 211 and 241 an all-soft GPU re-hardening (soft-to-rigid, after Yohei Nakajima's idea) merged two tilted bands into one V, seeded from the author's earlier 176 composition, from Evan Daniel's exact optimum of Joost de Winter's 211 and from Evan Daniel's exact optimum of Francisco Couzo's 241; at 304 the same re-hardening relaxed the author's composition of a 55-square (h + 8) x h piece and a 68-square (h + 7) x h piece without forming a V. The 211 replaces the author's issue-501 packing, registered as T-149, with a different one.

The README at the pin states that Francisco Couzo has improved the author's 156 to 12.979165853835 and the author's first 176 (13.808663234387) to 13.807637227056, each starting from the author's packing; those are Couzo's claims, not this source's.

The author reports that its own C++ checker (sqverify) accepts all four in GMP rational arithmetic and that a separate 80-digit mpmath cross-check accepts them; each side is reported as the exact first-order optimum of its contact topology with nonnegative KKT multipliers, reached by two routes that agree. These are author reports; no optimality is claimed.
